text: three engines perform well dataset (AUC > 0.98), reflecting fact tumor morphology highly predictive malignancy. Notably, logistic regression performs competitively flexible tree-based methods, reminder added model complexity always yield better clinical performance.

what: 5. Automated pipeline review: interpreting the leakage flag
title: Case Study: Breast Cancer Diagnosis
text: tr_agent_review() flags Cell.shape possible leakage concern, since alone achieves high AUC predicting malignancy. important nuance understand: check distinguish genuine, strong biological signal true data leakage (e.g. variable derived outcome ). case, cell shape well-established cytological indicator malignancy, leakage artifact. illustrates intended role tr_agent_review(): flags statistically unusual patterns human review, automatic disqualification. researcher domain knowledge can correctly interpret flag expected biological signal rather error.
code: bc_review <- tr_agent_review(bc_train, bc_model_glm, use_agent = FALSE) #>  #> --- triageR Pipeline Review --- #> [possible_leakage] #> Predictor 'Cell.shape' alone achieves AUC ~0.97 predicting the outcome. This may indicate data leakage (e.g. the variable is a proxy for or derived from the outcome).

title: Survival Analysis with triageR
text: every clinical outcome binary. Many research questions time event, time death, relapse, readmission, disease progression — patients followed full study others “censored” (event hasn’t happened time stop observing , leave study early). vignette walks triageR’s survival analysis workflow using classic lung dataset (survival package): time death patients advanced lung cancer.

title: Survival Analysis with triageR
text: lung dataset codes event status 1 (censored) / 2 (death), common convention older survival datasets, triageR expects standard 0/1 coding (0 = censored, 1 = event occurred).
code: lung_clean <- lung lung_clean$status <- lung_clean$status - 1 lung_clean <- lung_clean[stats::complete.cases(lung_clean), ]  head(lung_clean[, c("time", "status", "age", "sex", "ph.karno")]) #>   time status age sex ph.karno #> 2  455      1  68   1       90 #> 4  210      1  57   1       90 #> 6 1022      0  74   1       50 #> 7  310      1  68   2       70 #> 8  361      1  71   2       60 #> 9  218      1  53   1       70

title: Survival Analysis with triageR
text: triageR supports two survival engines interface used classification models: Cox Proportional Hazards (clinical standard, via survival engine) Random Survival Forest (via aorsf engine). Unlike tr_fit(), survival models fit tr_fit_survival(), expects time_col event_col instead single outcome column — reflecting different shape time--event data.
code: model_cox <- tr_fit_survival(   lung_clean,   time_col = "time",   event_col = "status",   engine = "cox_ph" ) #> Survival model fitted successfully using engine: cox_ph model_rf <- tr_fit_survival(   lung_clean,   time_col = "time",   event_col = "status",   engine = "survival_rf" ) #> Survival model fitted successfully using engine: survival_rf

title: Survival Analysis with triageR
text: Survival models validated tr_validate_survival(), computes concordance index (C-index) — survival analysis’s equivalent AUC. C-index 0.5 means model better chance ranking patient experience event sooner; 1.0 means perfect discrimination. example, Random Survival Forest achieves notably higher C-index Cox Proportional Hazards, suggesting relationship predictors survival time may fully linear log hazard scale, exactly kind finding motivates comparing one modelling approach.
code: val_cox <- tr_validate_survival(model_cox, newdata = lung_clean) #> Survival validation (training_data): #> C-index: 0.648 (SE: 0.03) #> N = 167, events = 120 #>  #> Interpretation: C-index of 0.5 = no better than chance; 1.0 = perfect discrimination between patients who experience the event sooner vs. later. val_rf <- tr_validate_survival(model_rf, newdata = lung_clean) #> Survival validation (training_data): #> C-index: 0.839 (SE: 0.018) #> N = 167, events = 120 #>  #> Interpretation: C-index of 0.5 = no better than chance; 1.0 = perfect discrimination between patients who experience the event sooner vs. later.

title: Survival Analysis with triageR
text: tr_agent_review() works survival models , adapting checks time--event context: instead class imbalance, checks event rate (proportion patients experienced event rather censored), events-per-variable calculated using number observed events rather total sample size.
code: review_cox <- tr_agent_review(lung_clean, model_cox, use_agent = FALSE) #>  #> --- triageR Pipeline Review --- #>  #> No major issues flagged.

title: Survival Analysis with triageR
text: tr_tripod_report() supports survival models via model_type argument. report adapts automatically: instead confusion matrix calibration plot, reports C-index standard error. Note: automated sensitivity analysis (tr_sensitivity()) currently supported classification models, survival models.
code: tr_tripod_report(   model = model_cox,   model_type = "survival",   validation = val_cox,   review = review_cox,   output_file = file.path(tempdir(), "lung_survival_report"),   format = "html" )

text: triageR provides streamlined, reproducible workflow building, validating, reporting clinical prediction models R. combines standard machine learning survival analysis tools optional AI agent recommends appropriate statistical methods, runs automated sensitivity analyses, flags common clinical modelling pitfalls. Reports generated format aligned TRIPOD+AI reporting guidance, support reproducible, guideline-conscious research. 📖 Full documentation function reference: https://devwebwacky.github.io/triageR/

title: Automated Machine Learning and AI Agent Tools for Clinical Prediction Modelling
text: R machine learning tooling (tidymodels, mlr3, caret) general-purpose. Clinical researchers left manually stitch together model fitting, validation, sensitivity analysis, explainability, TRIPOD-compliant reporting across many separate packages. triageR brings one coherent workflow, clinically-aware safeguards built , warning validation performed training data, flagging low events-per-variable ratios finalize model. AI agent layer entirely optional, every core function works without LLM/API key. agent adds method recommendations, plain language pipeline review summaries, assists sensitivity analysis interpretation, never required fit, validate, explain model.

title: Automated Machine Learning and AI Agent Tools for Clinical Prediction Modelling
text: example uses PIMA Indians Diabetes dataset demonstrate full triageR pipeline, raw data validated, explainable model.  See vignette("triageR-intro") full walkthrough, including model explainability, sensitivity analysis, engine comparison (logistic regression vs. random forest vs. boosted trees), TRIPOD+AI report generation.
code: library(triageR) library(MASS)  pima <- Pima.tr2 pima$id <- seq_len(nrow(pima))  pima_loaded <- tr_load_clinical(pima, id_col = "id") pima_imputed <- suppressMessages(tr_impute(pima_loaded[, setdiff(names(pima_loaded), "id")],                                             method = "mice", m = 5)) set.seed(42) train_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(pima_imputed)), size = floor(0.7 * nrow(pima_imputed))) train <- pima_imputed[train_idx, ] test  <- pima_imputed[-train_idx, ]  model <- tr_fit(train, outcome = "type", engine = "logistic_reg") #> Model fitted successfully using engine: logistic_reg validation <- tr_validate(model, newdata = test) #> Validation metrics (newdata): #> # A tibble: 5 × 3 #>   .metric     .estimator .estimate #>   <chr>       <chr>          <dbl> #> 1 roc_auc     binary         0.873 #> 2 sens        binary         0.742 #> 3 spec        binary         0.797 #> 4 accuracy    binary         0.778 #> 5 brier_score binary         0.142 #>  #> Confusion Matrix: #>           Truth #> Prediction No Yes #>        No  47   8 #>        Yes 12  23 review <- tr_agent_review(train, model, use_agent = FALSE) #>  #> --- triageR Pipeline Review --- #>  #> No major issues flagged.

what: Review a clinical modelling pipeline for common pitfalls — tr_agent_review
title: Review a clinical modelling pipeline for common pitfalls — tr_agent_review
text: Runs series rule-based checks common clinical-ML pitfalls (class imbalance low event rate, low events-per-variable, possible leakage, near-zero variance predictors), optionally asks LLM summarize findings plain language. Works binary classification models (triageR_model) survival models (triageR_survival_model).

title: Review a clinical modelling pipeline for common pitfalls — tr_agent_review
code: tr_agent_review(data, model, use_agent = TRUE)

title: Review a clinical modelling pipeline for common pitfalls — tr_agent_review
text: data data frame used fit model. model fitted triageR_model triageR_survival_model object. use_agent Logical. TRUE (default), also generates AI-written plain-language summary findings via ellmer.

title: Review a clinical modelling pipeline for common pitfalls — tr_agent_review
text: triageR_review object (list) containing tibble flags , use_agent = TRUE, AI-generated summary.

title: Review a clinical modelling pipeline for common pitfalls — tr_agent_review
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ tr_agent_review(data, model) } # }

what: Fit a clinical prediction model — tr_fit
title: Fit a clinical prediction model — tr_fit
text: Fits binary classification model using parsnip/workflows framework. user must specify model engine explicitly.

title: Fit a clinical prediction model — tr_fit
code: tr_fit(   data,   outcome,   engine = c("logistic_reg", "random_forest", "boost_tree"),   predictors = NULL )

title: Fit a clinical prediction model — tr_fit
text: data data frame containing predictors outcome column. outcome Character. Name binary outcome column (must factor coercible one, event interest second level). engine Character. Model engine use. One "logistic_reg", "random_forest", "boost_tree". predictors Character vector predictor column names. NULL (default), columns except outcome used.

title: Fit a clinical prediction model — tr_fit
text: fitted triageR_model object — list containing fitted workflow, engine used, outcome/predictor names.

title: Fit a clinical prediction model — tr_fit
code: set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(   age = round(rnorm(50, 55, 12)),   sex = sample(c("M", "F"), 50, replace = TRUE),   disease = sample(c(0, 1), 50, replace = TRUE) ) model <- tr_fit(df, outcome = "disease", engine = "logistic_reg") #> Model fitted successfully using engine: logistic_reg

what: Fits a survival model using the censored/parsnip framework. The outcome must be specified as separate time and event columns (following survival::Surv() convention), and the user must explicitly choose an engine. — tr_fit_survival
title: Fits a survival model using the censored/parsnip framework. The outcome must be specified as separate time and event columns (following survival::Surv() convention), and the user must explicitly choose an engine. — tr_fit_survival
text: Fits survival model using censored/parsnip framework. outcome must specified separate time event columns (following survival::Surv() convention), user must explicitly choose engine.

title: Fits a survival model using the censored/parsnip framework. The outcome must be specified as separate time and event columns (following survival::Surv() convention), and the user must explicitly choose an engine. — tr_fit_survival
code: tr_fit_survival(   data,   time_col,   event_col,   engine = c("cox_ph", "survival_rf"),   predictors = NULL )

title: Fits a survival model using the censored/parsnip framework. The outcome must be specified as separate time and event columns (following survival::Surv() convention), and the user must explicitly choose an engine. — tr_fit_survival
text: data data frame containing predictors, time column, event column. time_col Character. Name column giving time event censoring. event_col Character. Name column indicating event status (1 = event occurred, 0 = censored), following standard survival analysis convention. engine Character. One "cox_ph" (Cox Proportional Hazards) "survival_rf" (Random Survival Forest via aorsf engine). predictors Character vector predictor column names. NULL (default), columns except time_col event_col used.

title: Fits a survival model using the censored/parsnip framework. The outcome must be specified as separate time and event columns (following survival::Surv() convention), and the user must explicitly choose an engine. — tr_fit_survival
text: fitted triageR_survival_model object (list) containing fitted workflow, engine, time/event/predictor column names.

title: Fits a survival model using the censored/parsnip framework. The outcome must be specified as separate time and event columns (following survival::Surv() convention), and the user must explicitly choose an engine. — tr_fit_survival
code: if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(survival)   lung_clean <- lung   lung_clean$status <- lung_clean$status - 1  # convert 1/2 to 0/1   lung_clean <- lung_clean[stats::complete.cases(lung_clean), ]   model <- tr_fit_survival(lung_clean, time_col = "time",                             event_col = "status", engine = "cox_ph") } #> Survival model fitted successfully using engine: cox_ph

what: Launch the triageR Shiny app — tr_launch_app
title: Launch the triageR Shiny app — tr_launch_app
text: Opens interactive Shiny application building, validating, reporting clinical prediction models without writing R code directly. Supports data upload, model fitting across multiple engines, validation, explainability, automated pipeline review, TRIPOD+AI report generation. AI method-recommendation feature requires configured Gemini API key (see ?tr_recommend_method) optional.

title: Launch the triageR Shiny app — tr_launch_app
code: tr_launch_app()

title: Launch the triageR Shiny app — tr_launch_app
text: return; launches Shiny application.

title: Launch the triageR Shiny app — tr_launch_app
code: if (interactive()) {   tr_launch_app() }

what: Generate a TRIPOD+AI-aligned clinical model report — tr_tripod_report
title: Generate a TRIPOD+AI-aligned clinical model report — tr_tripod_report
text: Renders reproducible report summarizing model fit, validation, sensitivity analysis, pipeline review, aligned TRIPOD+AI reporting guidance. Supports binary classification survival models. drafting aid, certified compliance tool.

title: Generate a TRIPOD+AI-aligned clinical model report — tr_tripod_report
code: tr_tripod_report(   model,   model_type = c("classification", "survival"),   validation = NULL,   review = NULL,   sensitivity = NULL,   recommendation = NULL,   output_file = file.path(tempdir(), "triageR_report"),   format = c("html", "docx") )

title: Generate a TRIPOD+AI-aligned clinical model report — tr_tripod_report
text: model fitted triageR_model triageR_survival_model object. model_type Character. Either "classification" (default) "survival". Must match type model supplied. validation Optional validation object: triageR_validation (tr_validate()) classification models, triageR_survival_validation (tr_validate_survival()) survival models. review Optional triageR_review object tr_agent_review(). sensitivity Optional triageR_sensitivity object tr_sensitivity(). currently supported survival models. recommendation Optional character string tr_recommend_method(). output_file Character. File path (without extension) save report . Defaults file tempdir(). Set explicitly (e.g. file.path("my_folder", "report")) save elsewhere. format Character. Either "html" (default) "docx".

title: Generate a TRIPOD+AI-aligned clinical model report — tr_tripod_report
text: Invisibly returns path rendered report file.

what: Validate a clinical prediction model — tr_validate
title: Validate a clinical prediction model — tr_validate
text: Computes discrimination (AUC, sensitivity, specificity) calibration metrics fitted triageR_model. Can validate new (external/holdout) data, fall back training data clear warning.

title: Validate a clinical prediction model — tr_validate
code: tr_validate(   model,   newdata = NULL,   threshold = 0.5,   calibration_method = c("binned", "smooth") )

title: Validate a clinical prediction model — tr_validate
text: model fitted triageR_model object tr_fit(). newdata Optional data frame validate . NULL (default), validation runs original training data, warning. threshold Numeric. Probability threshold classifying positive class. Defaults 0.5. calibration_method Character. One "binned" (groups patients risk deciles, standard clinical approach) "smooth" (loess-smoothed calibration curve, granular). Defaults "binned".

title: Validate a clinical prediction model — tr_validate
text: triageR_validation object (list) containing metrics tibble underlying predictions, invisibly printed summary.

title: Validate a clinical prediction model — tr_validate
code: set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(   age = round(rnorm(50, 55, 12)),   sex = sample(c("M", "F"), 50, replace = TRUE),   disease = sample(c(0, 1), 50, replace = TRUE) ) model <- tr_fit(df, outcome = "disease", engine = "logistic_reg") #> Model fitted successfully using engine: logistic_reg tr_validate(model, newdata = df) #> Validation metrics (training_data): #> # A tibble: 5 × 3 #>   .metric     .estimator .estimate #>   <chr>       <chr>          <dbl> #> 1 roc_auc     binary         0.623 #> 2 sens        binary         0.364 #> 3 spec        binary         0.857 #> 4 accuracy    binary         0.64  #> 5 brier_score binary         0.236 #>  #> Confusion Matrix: #>           Truth #> Prediction  0  1 #>          0 24 14 #>          1  4  8

title: Validate a clinical survival model — tr_validate_survival
code: tr_validate_survival(model, newdata = NULL)

title: Validate a clinical survival model — tr_validate_survival
text: model fitted triageR_survival_model object tr_fit_survival(). newdata Optional data frame validate . NULL (default), validation runs original training data, warning.

title: Validate a clinical survival model — tr_validate_survival
text: triageR_survival_validation object (list) containing C-index supporting details.

title: Validate a clinical survival model — tr_validate_survival
code: if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(survival)   lung_clean <- lung   lung_clean$status <- lung_clean$status - 1   lung_clean <- lung_clean[stats::complete.cases(lung_clean), ]   model <- tr_fit_survival(lung_clean, time_col = "time",                             event_col = "status", engine = "cox_ph")   tr_validate_survival(model, newdata = lung_clean) } #> Survival model fitted successfully using engine: cox_ph #> Survival validation (training_data): #> C-index: 0.648 (SE: 0.03) #> N = 167, events = 120 #>  #> Interpretation: C-index of 0.5 = no better than chance; 1.0 = perfect discrimination between patients who experience the event sooner vs. later.

title: triageR 0.2.0
text: Added calibration plots (binned smoothed) Brier score tr_validate(), closing TRIPOD+AI reporting gap. New calibration_method argument ("binned" "smooth"). Calibration plot now included tr_tripod_report() output. Added robustness handling models limited probability variation (e.g. tree-based models many identical predictions). Added survival analysis support: tr_fit_survival() (Cox Proportional Hazards Random Survival Forest via censored/aorsf engines) tr_validate_survival() (concordance index / C-index). Added tr_launch_app(): interactive Shiny application full triageR workflow (upload data, fit compare models, validate, explain, review, download TRIPOD+AI report) without writing R code. Fixed test suite reliability issues related lazy-loaded survival datasets.
